name: Wanru Pang
title: PhD Candidate in Applied Linguistics
department: Department of Language Science and Technology
educationIntro: I hold an MA in Chinese Culture and Language from the National University of Singapore and a BA in Chinese Language and Literature from the University of Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.
bio: My research focuses on second-language writing development, language learning motivation, and identity, with particular attention to language learning and development among multilingual and Chinese L2 learners in sociocultural contexts. I use mixed methods, combining qualitative interviews with quantitative analysis to examine Chinese L2 learners’ writing development and individual differences through linguistic features, individual psychological factors, and sociocultural influences.

projects.title: First-language proficiency and English reading comprehension among upper-primary multilingual learners in British Columbia
projects.funding: Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council of Canada
details: Conduct semi-structured interviews with parents and children on bilingual literacy development, home language practices, and family support for first- and second-language learning; transcribe and verify Mandarin interviews to prepare qualitative data for thematic analysis.
Help review and refine parent and child interview protocols to align with the project’s longitudinal mixed-methods design.
Conduct classroom observations to document multilingual learners’ language use, reading comprehension support, classroom participation, and teacher feedback in English reading classes.

projects.title: Motivation, engagement and task performance in L2 Chinese integrated writing among non-Chinese-speaking students: developmental trajectories and longitudinal associations
projects.funding: General Research Fund, Research Grants Council of Hong Kong
details: Coordinate implementation of a longitudinal mixed-methods project on L2 Chinese integrated writing, including pilot testing, instrument development, school-based data collection, and coordination of qualitative and quantitative analysis.

Lead the qualitative component: develop interview frameworks, semi-structured protocols and coding schemes; conduct in-depth interviews in English with secondary CSL learners and thematic analysis in NVivo.

Lead the quantitative component: design questionnaires and integrated writing tasks, coordinate data collection over four years, liaise with participating schools, assess writing tasks, clean datasets and assist with analysis.
Prepare journal manuscripts reporting the project’s qualitative and quantitative findings.

projects.title: Undergraduate students’ peer- and self-initiated feedback on academic writing: feedback patterns and strategies
details: Conducted literature reviews and assisted with data collection; carried out interviews, focus groups and transcription of audio recordings.
Assisted with data analysis, including confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modelling, and other project research tasks.
